catalog_quote: Braun and Crofts (1965; also Crofts 1973, 1985) analyzed the language as having four opposing tone levels, three of tone and one of laryngealization (i.e. creaky voice) – accent 1 is a super-high tone, accent 2 a high level tone, accent 3 a low level tone, and accent 4 is creakiness. In this chapter (see also Picanço 1997, 2002a-c), I defend the hypothesis that the tone system of Mundurukú can be analyzed as having only two opposing levels: Low and High (hereafter L and H respectively). ... These five tonal behaviors are accounted for by assuming a four-way lexical distinction: a mora, the tone-bearing unit, may be lexically specified for H, L, or none; that is, it may be toneless (Section 8.2). Lexical H tones are stable, and lexical L tones trigger dissimilation of a following L; toneless moras get L tone by default, but this tone is inert. Unstable H tones and tonal polarity are expl…

audit.reasoning: Quote check: all deciding passages are verbatim in the held Picanço 2005 text at the stated sections and pages (8.1 p. 310 / PDF 324; 8.2 p. 311 / PDF 325; 4.4.2 PDF 134). Deciding source is a 410-pp phonology dissertation with instrumental tone data by the language's main phonologist, the best available and the work every later description defers to. Three open later sources fetched sources now (Picanço 2012 teaching monograph pp. 35-36; Santos 2013 UnB MA p. 107; Gomes 2006 UnB PhD pp. 8-9) all state Mundurukú is tonal with two contrastive tones (H/L), laryngealized vowels L-only, and none describes word stress; 'acento' appears only as diacritic names or a generic clitic definition. Web search found no stress/rhythm study or JIPA illustration for Mundurukú. Coding 'tonal', domain UNSTATED, no stress rule, stands. sources.citation: Gomes, Dioney Moreira (2006). Estudo Morfológico e Sintático da Língua Mundurukú (Tupí). Tese de Doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. xix+265 pp.
sources.quote: Cites Crofts (1971:79) four tones vs Picanço (2005:12) two levels, quoting Picanço's abstract; 'Por ser a carga funcional dos tons muito pequena, eles não serão marcados ao longo desta tese.' Only other 'acento' uses are the generic Zwicky/Halpern clitic definition (p. 25: person markers 'desprovidos de acento próprio'); no Mundurukú stress rule given.

sources.citation: Picanço, Gessiane Lobato (2012). Introdução ao Mundurukú: fonética, fonologia e ortografia. Cadernos de Etnolingüística, Série Monografias 3. 74 pp.
sources.quote: 'O Mundurukú é uma língua tonal (Braun & Crofts 1965; Picanço 2002, 2005)... A língua possui dois tons contrastivos: o tom Alto (A)... e o tom Baixo (B)... Os únicos segmentos que podem carregar o tom em Mundurukú são as vogais... A forma como os tons A e B serão combinados em uma sequência é imprevisível' (all 4 disyllabic and all 8 trisyllabic H/L patterns attested; laryngealized vowels only L). No word stress/acento de intensidade is described anywhere in the monograph ('acento' occurs only as 'acento agudo/grave' = diacritics).

sources.citation: Santos, Cássia Alessandra Braga dos (2013). Aspectos da fonologia do Mundurukú do Madeira (AM). Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade de Brasília. 127 pp.
sources.quote: 'O mundurukú é uma língua tonal... Em Mundurukú do Madeira (AM), identificamos dois tons, o tom alto e o tom baixo... Uma generalização possível é que as vogais laringalizadas têm tom baixo. Um estudo detalhado de tom poderia ainda ser feito.' Segmental + syllable study of the Madeira variety; no stress/acento discussed.
